exact_statement: Let a finite actual query/reset tree on a uniform Boolean cube have path query count T, a fixed signed root character c transported through the SAME input affine maps and output characters, error event Z={f!=c}, e=P(Z), dbar=E T and a=E[T 1_Z]. Its exact depth-law occupation envelope is A(e,T)=min over integers L=0,...,max T of L e+E(T-L)_+, and a<=A(e,T). The envelope is sharp over error events of the prescribed mass on the same original uniform inputs: choose the e*N largest-depth inputs, realizing an actual Boolean error event against constant1. An upper-tail selection and a threshold L give exact rational primal/dual certificates, including ties and e0/e1. With phi(x)=h2(x)+2x/ln2, dbar>0, the complete entropy decrement is at most dbar phi(min(2A(e,T)/dbar,1/2)); zero-query trees have zero decrement. For families with e->0 and uniformly integrable depth laws the entropy decrement tends0. Under a uniform finite bound on E T, e E T^2->0 is a sufficient alternative. The canonical activated-tensor control-first/all-active-data tree attains A=a=e(k+dt), so bounded expected depth alone cannot supply vanishing occupation or inherited-deficit admission. No claim makes the entropy bound itself sharp or selects a universally paid original pair.
hypotheses: Finite uniform actual Boolean input/query trees; complete original input path depths retained
Any fixed signed root character transported through the same affine input/output-character maps
Sharpness concerns the occupation envelope over error events, not the entropy bound or best-character eligibility
Uniform integrability or bounded mean plus e E T^2->0 is additional; bounded expected depth alone is insufficient
proof_dependencies: Elementary upper-tail threshold duality, finite conditional counting and Cauchy--Schwarz
